description:
A helper `async fn make_space(backend: &MemoryBackend, name: &str) -> String` exists at crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/integration.rs:3253 and is called 26 times — but the file (6643 lines, 30+ Space-create call sites) contains many older tests above line 3253 that inline the same boilerplate:

    let (create_resp, _) = handle_space_set(
        &backend,
        &(),
        json!({ "accountId": "a1", "create": { "s0": { "name": "..." } } }),
    )
    .await
    .expect("create");
    let space_id = create_resp["created"]["s0"]["id"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("id")
        .to_owned();

Call sites include integration.rs:296-309, 363-376, 400-413, 2674-2686, 2833-2843, 2868-2878, 2926-2937, 2988-2998 and ~22 more before line 3253.

Same Chat-create-then-get-id pattern repeats too (integration.rs:294-309, 366-376, 400-413) — no `make_chat` helper exists. No `make_emoji` helper either.

Idiomatic Rust: hoist `make_space`, `make_chat`, `make_emoji`, etc. into tests/common/mod.rs (per JMAP-x2gd.80) and rewrite the inline boilerplate to call them. Cases that need a non-default kind or owner take parameters.

Engineering basis: the crate's own contributor wrote `make_space` and then forgot to retrofit ~30 earlier tests. Each inline block is 12-14 lines of JSON-shape gymnastics that obscure the actual subject of the test. When a test fails, a reader spends time decoding 'did this fail because the create failed or because the assertion under test failed?'. Lifted helpers also enforce uniform `.expect("create space")` diagnostic messages across files.

Combined with JMAP-x2gd.80 and JMAP-x2gd.81, this is one of three related test-shape findings: the dedup pass for all three is a single coordinated commit that lifts seed_space + make_space + ACCOUNT_ID/SPACE_ID consts into tests/common/mod.rs.
title: tests: make_space helper exists at integration.rs:3253 but ~30 older inline blocks still hand-roll the same 14-line boilerplate; no make_chat / make_emoji helpers
